Name: Casa Lac
Tips: Spain's oldest restaurant license (est. 1825). Classic Aragonese cuisine in a beautiful historic room. Ternasco al horno (roast lamb) and migas aragonesas. NO Monday dinner (listings say closed Mon) — our slot is Tue Sep 1 lunch 13:30. Reserve: 976 39 61 96 or restaurantecasalac@gmail.com.

Name: El Chalet
Address: C/ de Santa Teresa de Jesús 25 Zaragoza
Tips: One of Zaragoza's best restaurants for contemporary cooking with local Aragonese ingredients. Tasting menu or à la carte seasonal dishes. Book ahead. Didn't win a slot on this 1-night stop.

Name: La Rinconada de Lorenzo
Tips: Classic Aragonese home cooking. The ternasco asado and Pyrenean trout are outstanding. Normally closed Sun night + Mon, and reported closed for holidays through August — call 976 55 51 08 before relying on it Sep 1.

Name: El Temple pintxos street
Tips: Zaragoza's second pintxos row — lower-key and very local. Go 20:30–22:00. Overflow plan if El Tubo is rammed.

Name: Mercado de las Artes
Address: C/ de San Ignacio de Loyola Zaragoza
Tips: Food hall listed at this address — but listings are inconsistent (appears elsewhere as Mercado Gastronómico). Confirm it's open before relying on it; Mercado Central and El Tubo are the verified alternatives.

Name: Bar El Fútbol
Tips: Classic Aragonese bar breakfast — tostada con tomate, coffee, atmosphere. A local institution; humble, authentic. Tuesday 08:30 breakfast option — verify hours on site.

Name: Pastelería Fantoba
Tips: Zaragoza's most famous pastry house since 1856 — Egyptian-revival interior. Trenza de Almudévar is the city's signature sweet. Open daily 10:00–22:00 (too late for breakfast). Buy two Tue afternoon: one with coffee, one for the AVE.

Name: Bar Gallizo
Tips: Excellent tapas recommended by Airbnb host. Casual neighborhood favourite — 5 min walk from Calle Dr. Alejandro Palomar. Monday/late-August hours unverified — El Tubo is the fallback.

Name: Restaurante El Fuelle
Tips: Traditional Aragonese bodega-museum with wood-fired oven, recommended by Airbnb host — 3 min from the apartment. CLOSED Mondays; Tue–Sat 12–16 and 20–24. Our Casa Lac backup for Tue lunch — reserve 976 39 80 33.

Name: El Ángel del Pincho
Tips: Pajaritos (small fried birds) and tempura — pintxos-style. Host recommendation. Right next to Bar La Viña for an easy two-stop crawl.

Name: Bar La Viña
Tips: Berenjenas con miel (eggplant with honey) is the signature dish. Host recommendation. Adjacent to El Ángel del Pincho.

Name: The Lynx
Tips: Local atmospheric bar where Guardia Civil hangs out. Host pick — very neighbourhood, no tourists. Nightcap stop on the way home.

Name: Bodegas Almau
Tips: El Tubo classic since 1870 — original woodwork, vermouth on tap, famous anchovy pintxos (try anchovy with tomato jam). Open Mon–Sun 11–16 and 19–24 — a verified Monday anchor for Aug 31.

Name: Taberna Doña Casta
Tips: The croqueta institution of Zaragoza — get the ternasco croqueta and a mixed board. Open Mon–Sun 12–16 and 19:30–24 — verified Monday-open for Aug 31 dinner crawl.

Name: El Champi
Tips: One-dish wonder: the grilled-mushroom pintxo with garlic and oil on a bread base. Order in multiples of four. Opposite Doña Casta in El Tubo.

Name: El Cachirulo
Tips: Zaragoza has NO tourist flamenco tablao — Aragón's music is the jota. This is the big folklore restaurant that runs live jota singing and dancing in full regional costume with dinner. WARNING: 15-min taxi out of the centre and shows lean to weekends — call first. A Monday performance (our only evening) is unlikely.
